lines.en: Over the past 3 years, much had changed for Jung Heewon.
―Jung Heewon, leader of the Chungcheong Alliance!
―The Supreme King's era is over! The strongest incarnation is the Evil Slayer (滅惡)!

She had a fan club, and people in various media outlets had begun looking to turn her exploits into articles or adapt them into stories they could sell. Every incarnation who wielded a sword admired her. Some constellations even tried to recruit her into their nebulas.
Of course, those efforts were pointless. Jung Heewon was already the incarnation of a constellation who was exceptionally famous even in the <Star Stream>.
The problem was that this famous sponsor had not appeared before Jung Heewon for a full 3 years.
“I thought my sponsor had died.”

Her sponsor had abruptly vanished after the incident 3 years ago. That left Jung Heewon no choice but to work harder than other incarnations. Day after day, she endured grueling training at the hands of transcendents like the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and Kyrgios.
So she would not fall behind her companions, so she would never have to sacrifice anyone again.
“If that had actually happened, at least I'd feel a little less wronged.”
Jung Heewon had truly grown strong.
And after she had grown strong, her missing sponsor appeared before her.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ remains silent.]
Jung Heewon sighed.
“And on top of that······ what did you just say to me?”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ giggles.]
Jung Heewon did not smile.
She simply placed a hand quietly on the grip of her sword.
[Incarnation ‘Jung Heewon’ is preparing to activate ‘Hour of Judgement’!]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is startled!]
Murderous magic power settled into Jung Heewon's sword.
[The constellations of Absolute Good have agreed to Jung Heewon's request!]
[One constellation of Absolute Good has opposed the request!]
[Skill activation is canceled!]
Jung Heewon frowned.
‘Hour of Judgement’ was a skill activated through the consent of constellations of Absolute Good.
And her sponsor was one of the highest-ranking constellations of ‘Absolute Good.’
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ looks ready to cry.]
Jung Heewon took her hand off her sword and sighed again.
Her sponsor's emotions flowed into her mind, just as they were.
Sorrow and joy.
Regret and guilt.
The truth was, Jung Heewon knew too.
Why Uriel had been forced to remain in confinement for the past 3 years.
After what had happened in the ‘Demon King Selection,’ it was actually surprising that <Eden> had let her off with nothing more than confinement.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says she is sorry.]
But hurt feelings were still hurt feelings.
Especially when what her sponsor had to say after 3 years away was······.
“If you want to see Dokja-ssi, why don't you go see him yourself? You know perfectly well he's at the top of the fortress.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says she cannot summon her symbolic body because her probation period has not yet ended.]
Jung Heewon thought it over, hesitating for a long time before speaking.
“······All right. But don't do anything strange.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is overjoyed!]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ asks if Kim Dokja really is being held captive.]
“······Why are you happy about that?”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ asks if Kim Dokja really did become a squid, though.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’······.]
“We're on our way, so see for yourself.”
Before long, Jung Heewon reached the top of the fortress where Kim Dokja was being held.
[The Heavenly Emperor's Barrier (天帝結界) has been applied to this space.]
[Incarnation ‘Jung Heewon’ is authorized to enter.]
The door opened to reveal a luxurious room. They called it captivity, but the room could put a suite in most 5-star hotels to shame.

A lavish feast had been laid out on the table, ready for him to help himself whenever he was hungry, and a skill that helped him sleep soundly had been cast on the king-size bed. Several fantasy novels published before the world's ruin were stacked on a small bedside table. Come to think of it, hadn't Kim Dokja said he liked fantasy novels?
Jung Heewon picked one up out of curiosity. 『The Sekai After the Fall』. By singShangShong······.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ screams!]
When she turned her head, she saw Kim Dokja sitting in a cushioned rocking chair. His sleeve was rolled up, and a catheter had been inserted for a Story pack infusion.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ gazes at the ‘Demon King of Salvation.’]
The pack contained a generous dose of the sedative Lee Seolhwa had made. As she approached, she could see the face of Kim Dokja, sprawled in the chair.
Under her steady gaze, Kim Dokja blearily opened his eyes.
“······Heewon-ssi?”
Jung Heewon bit her lip without realizing it.
Kim Dokja's unguarded face, worn out by hard times.
A sharp pang struck a corner of her heart.
“Where in the world······?”
There had been so much she wanted to say when she saw Kim Dokja again.

She had wanted to get angry, to pour out her resentment, to demand why on earth he had done such a thing. But for some reason, the moment she saw his face like this, all those feelings began melting away like snow.
Whether these were her own feelings.
Or her sponsor's—Jung Heewon couldn't quite tell.
Jung Heewon adjusted the amount of sedative flowing through the catheter.
“There's someone······ no, an angel who wants to see you, Dokja-ssi.”
Pure white light flowed from Jung Heewon's hand.
The comforting light of an archangel, reminiscent of the light at the beginning of time.
Jung Heewon lifted Kim Dokja into her arms and laid him on the bed.
Before long, Kim Dokja fell asleep, his breathing soft and even. Jung Heewon's hand, shrouded in white radiance, brushed his hair back several times.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ gazes at the ‘Demon King of Salvation.’]
Some feelings are all the more precious because words cannot convey them.
Until now, Jung Heewon had never quite understood Uriel's ‘camaraderie,’ but somehow, at this moment, she felt she understood a little.
I had a long dream.
It was a slightly strange dream.
―Vital signs look good.
―The Story pack infusion is proceeding steadily.
The voices of Lee Seolhwa and Aileen reaching me like auditory hallucinations.
Sometimes I saw Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung's faces as they clung to my waist.
―Waaaaaah! Dokja-ssiiii!
Sometimes I heard Lee Hyunsung's voice howling like a monster.
I thought I might have caught a glimpse of my mother's face, too.
I thought.
If this was a dream, I'd rather not wake up.
―Hey, he's waking up! Hurry up and give him the sedative!
Hearing Han Sooyoung's faint voice, I let out a small chuckle.
In a way, this dream was a play put on for me alone.
Just as ‘Ways of Survival’ had been for me.
「In truth, Kim Dokja could wake whenever he wished, but he did not get up.」
And so I gladly decided to become the audience for that play.
「For the first time since the ruin began, Kim Dokja slept peacefully.」
I had never felt anything like it. My heart, which had always been so restless. The knowledge that someone could protect me. That there were people who believed in what I believed in, too.
―Get plenty of rest, Dokja-ssi.
······Right. There was still a little time before scenario 46.
The moment I let myself relax, a fathomless sleep swept over me.
Held by the scruff of his neck, Lee Gilyoung shouted.
“Aw, noona! Did I really have to come here too? I want to spend more time with Dokja-hyung!”
“You've spent plenty of time with him already.”
“Shin Yoosung got eight whole hours with him! I only got six!”
Lee Jihye rapped her knuckles on Lee Gilyoung's head as he stuck out his lips, looking sulky.

“Their air superiority (制空力) is a pain. You and Yoosung are the only ones who can deal with them, aren't you? Besides, we've put Dokja ajusshi into a deep sleep, so you can see him whenever you want.”
“Unnie, we're almost there.”

At Shin Yoosung's words, the [Chimera Dragon] began a steep descent. The buildings of the ‘Gyeonggi Alliance’ came into view below. There was a simple reason they had come here despite being responsible for the ‘Busan Alliance.’
“······They said they'd set up some kingdom. Guess it was true.”
The province's residents, treated like slaves, were crying out in pain.
Lee Jihye's lips twitched as she spoke.
“Let's smash it all.”
As Lee Jihye drew her sword, Lee Gilyoung stepped forward and spoke.
“Hey, Shin Yoosung. I'll handle this, so stay out of it.”
“Shut up. You couldn't even recognize Dokja ajusshi.”
“······Go, Titano―MKⅡ!”
Groooooar!
At Lee Gilyoung's command, a squad of creatures of the insect king species came flying through the sky, clad in sturdy armor.
There were no fewer than five grade 4 creatures of the insect king species.
“We're under attack!”
Slaaash!
Watching the buildings being sliced apart by the giant mantis's scythes, Lee Jihye asked.
“Didn't you say Titano died?”
“That one was just Titano. This one's Titano―MKⅡ.”
“What difference does that even······?”
Boooooom!

An explosion erupted in the heart of the enemy camp. It wasn't the area Titano had attacked. The high-rise buildings that formed the core of the Gyeonggi Alliance were collapsing, sending out tremendous shock waves. Airships floating in the sky were struck by sword aura that fell like lightning and came crashing down.
Lee Jihye spoke in disbelief.
“We were told to handle it ourselves······.”
Only ruins remained where the tempest had swept through.
A man slaughtering the alliance's underlings as they scrambled to flee.
It was Yoo Joonghyuk.
“W-wait! Just a moment! Stop, Supreme King!”
A man who appeared to be an officer of the Gyeonggi Alliance shouted frantically.
“You'll be in trouble if you kill me now! We have a hostage!”
At the word ‘hostage,’ Yoo Joonghyuk's blade hesitated for the first time.
Apparently thinking it had worked, the man kept shouting.
“Phew······ I hear the Moonlight Empress (月下賢帝) hasn't left the top floor of the fortress because of a worsening illness?”
Bewildered, Lee Jihye and Shin Yoosung turned to look at each other.
“What's that bastard talking about?”
“······The Moonlight Empress is Sangah-unnie, isn't she?”
The man continued.
“Haha, it took us ages to breach the Demon Realm's defenses, but we finally did it!”
“······What nonsense is this?”

“Our alliance's elite raiding squad has infiltrated the fortress in your absence. In other words, the Moonlight Empress's life is now in our hands. Breaking through the barrier was quite difficult, but your companion's life is now in our hands―”
“You broke through the barrier?”
For the first time, Yoo Joonghyuk's composure cracked. The same expression soon spread across the others' faces. Shin Yoosung spoke.
“······But Sangah-unnie's room doesn't have a barrier, does it?”
“Then what that lunatic is talking about······.”
They all turned toward Seoul at once.
At that same moment, ten raiders were inside the fortress of the [Industrial Complex], having infiltrated it by dropping from high altitude.
They were all elite members of the ‘Gyeonggi Alliance’ raiding squad.
―So this is the place.
―Yes, that's right.
―Dispel team, get started.
At their leader's command, the squad members responsible for dispelling the enchantment rushed forward. One of them asked.
―The Black Flames Demon Ruler isn't here, right? Our officers got slaughtered in droves last time, didn't they?
It had not been long since the Black Flames Empress's nickname changed to the Black Flames Demon Ruler, and the Moonlight Goddess's to the Moonlight Empress.
It was all because of the ‘Seongnam Catastrophe’ 1 year ago.
―The Black Flames Demon Ruler is away. It's the Moonlight Empress in there.
―Will we be enough on our own?
―Rumor has it she's gravely ill. If that woman's alone, there won't be a problem.
A short while later, the enchantment blocking the door was undone.
―Dispelling complete!
―Already? That was faster than I expected.
―Well, the Heavenly Emperor's Barrier is hard to break through from the inside, but it's easy from the outside.
―Ridiculous. What sort of barrier is that?
―Exactly, sir. How stupid······.
Leaving the chuckling squad member behind him, the leader opened the door.
―Let's see what this great ‘Moonlight Empress’ can do. Everyone, prepare to enter!
But the moment he touched the doorknob, an unexpected message invaded their ears.
[The constellation ‘Assassin of the Black Wasteland’ cries out a warning!]
[The constellation ‘Hunter of the Black Moon’ is horrified!]
[The constellation ‘Knight of the Frozen Heart’ convulses.]
They were all their sponsors.
―What the hell is this? All of a sudden, my sponsor······.
―D-did you hear that too, Squad Leader-nim?
Their confusion did not last long. A terrifying display of Status could be felt beyond the door. An unfathomable aura unlike anything they had ever encountered was binding their entire bodies.
―My body······?
Every raider's feet froze before a Status on an entirely different level.
It was impossible.
“······I was finally getting some proper rest. Just my luck.”
Through the creaking door, a man in a white coat was walking out. Smiling, he set a cool palm firmly on the squad leader's shoulder.
“Thank you for letting me out, everyone.”
It took less than thirty seconds from that moment for nine of the raiders to be laid out on the floor.
After sealing the pressure points of all the groaning raiders, I dusted off my hands. Checking a few of their profiles through [Character List] gave me the answer without any need to pry.
“······The Gyeonggi Alliance. Now, what brings you here?”
Fssssss.
The bodies of several raiders who had bitten into poison pills before I could seal their pressure points melted away. It seemed they had been placed under Suggestion.
[The constellation ‘Assassin of the Black Wasteland’ is wary of you!]
[The constellation ‘Hunter of the Black Moon’ questions the fairness of the scenario!]
When I frowned into the air, all the messages subsided at once.
I carefully examined the raiders' appearance and the route they had used to enter.
Beyond the broken window, I saw one of them fleeing through the air.
Whoooooosh―!
From the movement technique he used to run through the air, I had an idea who he was.
I'd thought they were ordinary raiders. To think one of the 10 Evils (十惡) had been among them.
The leader of the Gyeonggi Alliance, Cho Jinchul of the 10 Evils.
With a Murim master of an earlier generation as his sponsor, he had originally been one of scenario 45's headaches.
Of course, that was only according to the original novel. He wasn't worth worrying about now. Even among the 10 Evils there were different levels, and Cho Jinchul was one of the small fry.
With my companions as they were now, there would be no incarnation on the Korean Peninsula who could match them. The United States or India might be another matter······.
“There he is! After him!”
I saw several people chasing Cho Jinchul as he receded into the distance. Among them was the returnee Flying Fox, whom I had brought with me.
As the fugitive fled and his pursuers gave chase, an unobstructed view of Seoul opened up before me.
The Seoul I knew so well.
And the [Industrial Complex] occupying its center.

Through my contract with the ‘Secretive Plotter,’ the [Industrial Complex] had been transported to the empty city of Seoul. Looking at that landscape, as though reality and a novel had merged, made me feel anew how much the world had changed.
Directly below the fortress, enormous letters spelled out ‘Yoo Joonghyuk―Kim Dokja Industrial Complex.’
······Why did Yoo Joonghyuk come first?
I'd have to change that later.
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ looks at you.]
I looked up into the air.
Guardian of Youths and Travel.
I knew who that modifier belonged to.
“Raphael.”
Raphael, an archangel of the nebula <Eden>.
Bzzzzzt······!
Sparks flew in the air as if in response to the true name.
I'd thought it was about time <Eden> contacted me.
“I was just planning to visit you. There's something I need to return······.”
I thought of Gabriel's symbolic body, which should still be inside my coat.
Jophiel's restraints should have begun losing their effect by now, so it was about time Gabriel woke up. But······.
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ says Gabriel has already been retrieved.]
The lily inside my coat was gone.

Come to think of it, I seemed to remember an archangel's touch brushing over me in my sleep. Perhaps one of <Eden>'s constellations had visited then. Since Jung Heewon's sponsor was Uriel, Uriel was the most likely possibility.
······Speaking of which, what had happened to Uriel?
Why hadn't she sent any indirect messages even though I'd shown up?
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ says Uriel has not yet been granted permission to speak in the channel.]
Ah, so that was it.
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ indicates that he has a question for you.]
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ says the ‘Red Cosmos’ has not returned.]
At Raphael's message, I hesitated briefly before speaking.
“······The ‘Commander of the Red Cosmos’ could not return with me.”
Jophiel, the Commander of the Red Cosmos.
Without her help, I would not have been able to return to the third round's worldline.
“She wanted to remain in another worldline, of her own free will.”
A violent gale swept through the area.
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ distrusts your words!]
Bzzzzzzzt······!
It was the will of an enraged Raphael. I calmly continued.
“With your abilities, you should know that I'm not lying.”
Before long, the wind swirling around me began to subside.
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ looks at you.]
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ requests an explanation.]
“I intend to give you one. Scenario 46 is coming up······ so I'll be able to tell you in person soon.”
I felt a subtle change in the way Raphael was looking at me.
That archangel must know what that scenario is, too.
“I'll visit <Eden> as soon as the scenario is over.”
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ replies that he will be waiting.]
With that final message, Raphael's presence in the surrounding air vanished completely. The space that had been flooded with Status was suddenly empty, leaving a bitter feeling.

Accumulating countless Stories, I had become quite strong. I now possessed enough Status to overwhelm lower- and mid-tier Historical-grade constellations, and finding an incarnation stronger than me would be nearly impossible.
Even so, the archangel's ‘Status’ still towered far beyond my reach.
Raphael, Guardian of Youths and Travel.
The archangel who had defeated the powerful Demon King ‘Asmodeus.’
「Kim Dokja quietly clenched and unclenched his fist.」

I still had a long way to go. But there was no need to rush. I was doing well enough already. Speaking of Asmodeus······ no, what had happened to Department Head Han? So much had happened while I was away that I had more than a few questions.
First, I checked my system messages.
[You have a missed Dokkaebi Communication.]
[Sender: High-grade Dokkaebi Bihyung]
It was a message from Bihyung.
I'd thought it strange that Bihyung hadn't made a fuss about my return······ apparently, he'd planned to make do with a message like this.
I used the screen to open the message window.
The message was long, but its contents were simple.
Sorry I couldn't come see you.
There are a few things keeping me busy.
I'll come see you as soon as they're done.
That was more or less the gist of the lengthy message.
―But don't you take proper care of your own kid?
The news I'd been wondering about only appeared at the end of the message.
―Biyoo's with me. Well, she's my child too. You left her in front of the portal, and the Wenny men nearly took her.
I'd already been growing worried because Biyoo hadn't shown up.
―You'll be in for a surprise when she comes back. Look forward to it.
That was how Bihyung's message ended.
Something about it left me uneasy, but knowing Biyoo was with Bihyung still put my mind a little more at ease.
Well, time to get moving.
After piling the fallen raiders in one place, I decided to find my companions first.
And some ten minutes later.
I was wandering around, lost.
······Had the [Factory] always been this big?

I scratched my head and looked around, but I couldn't work out where anything was. It was enough to make me wonder whether I should buy and learn [Map Reading] or [Pathfinding] now, while it still wasn't too late.
“Hello? Is anyone here?”

I had a particular tendency to get lost in ‘buildings I was visiting for the first time.’ When I first started elementary school and middle school, when I was first assigned to my military unit, and when I joined Mino Soft······.
Come to think of it, that was also why I'd first spoken to Yoo Sangah.
「······Kim Dokja thought. ‘Where the hell is the emergency exit?’」
I'd never properly explored the Factory's interior while I was in the Demon Realm, so I could hardly tell where anything was. Even the layout seemed to have changed since then.
For now, I decided to open the doors of any rooms that looked promising, one by one.
Hissssss!
The moment I opened a door, a small tentacled monster and some frogs turned to look at me.
Some specimens were inside test tubes, while others roamed freely around the room.
<Frog That Was Almost Dokja Ajusshi>
<Elephant Monster That Was Nearly Dokja Ajusshi>
<Tentacled Monster That Sadly Wasn't Dokja Ajusshi>
A frog tilted its head at me, then shot out its tongue with a swish.
Startled, I shut the door.
······Wait a second. This room couldn't be······.
I was about to check the nameplate on the door when I heard a voice nearby.
“······Hey! How did you get out?”
“Dokja-ssi?”
It was Lee Hyunsung and Han Sooyoung, carrying a meal.
“So, Dokja-ssi. Back in scenario 35, I······.”
Lee Hyunsung was giving me a lengthy account of the scenarios he'd been through. As I listened quietly, I closely examined every part of his body.
Pectoral muscles more developed than before. And the magic power of steel linking his muscle fibers together.
Lee Hyunsung had now become proficient in [Steel Transformation].
A level that would let him begin scenario 46 right away without any difficulty.
I was a little moved.
Even in my absence, my companions had faithfully kept training according to the guidelines I had given them.
Of course, listening to Lee Hyunsung's story wasn't all I was doing.
[‘Midday Tryst’ is active.]
[Incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’ is currently participating in the conversation.]
It was fortunate that I'd been able to meet Han Sooyoung first.
No matter how early you prepared for a scenario, it was always too late.
To prepare quickly, I needed someone who could efficiently give me the most precise information, and only one person stood out as the best fit.
―Where are Jang Hayoung and the Breaking the Sky Sword Master?
―They went to another scenario region with the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and Kyrgios. I think they went to get a scenario exclusively for transcendents.
―What about Han Myungoh and Gong Pildu?

―They're in North Korea right now. Gong Pildu went to do the North Korean scenarios and scout out some land while he was at it. Han Myungoh was waiting to see which way things went and got dragged along too.
······North Korea, huh.
Well, it was about time the North Korean incarnations started running wild too.
Quite a few formidable constellations would be gathered in North Korea by now. Most would be Historical-grade, of course, but some could rival Narrative-grade constellations.
The Great King (太王), for instance······.
―Where have you been all this time?
―The worldline of Ways of Survival's 1863rd round.
Han Sooyoung's eyes went wide.
―What? Seriously?
―Oh, you were there too. Though I don't know which of you is the original.
―······The original? What kind of bullshit is that?
Just as I was about to answer, someone stepped into our path.
“······Dokja-ssi.”
It was Jung Heewon.
“I slept well, thanks to you.”

Jung Heewon looked at me with complicated emotions in her eyes. She seemed to want to say something, or perhaps, on the contrary, to hear what I had to say. Her gaze slowly shifted toward Han Sooyoung.

For an instant, something like a sharp electrical current sparked between Han Sooyoung and Jung Heewon. After glaring coldly at Han Sooyoung, Jung Heewon turned her head. In the awkward atmosphere, I spoke first.
“Oh, there were some intruders earlier, so outside my room······.”
“I've ordered someone to deal with them. Now that you're awake, go see Sangah-ssi. We can talk about the details afterward.”
Her voice was far colder than usual. It was enough to make me wonder if this was the Jung Heewon I knew. Beside me, Lee Hyunsung watched her walk away with a strangely sorrowful look in his eyes.
After Jung Heewon rounded the corner and disappeared, I asked Han Sooyoung.
“What's going on?”
“What?”
“What's going on between you and Jung Heewon-ssi?”
Watching Han Sooyoung pout, I grew a little frustrated. I didn't know what had happened, but this was no time for the two of them to fight.
“Have you forgotten scenario 46 is coming up? Right now, you······.”
“You weren't here for 3 years. If you don't know what happened, shut up.”
With those words, Han Sooyoung also spun around and stalked away.
Suddenly, only Lee Hyunsung and I remained.
Seeing Lee Hyunsung's slumped shoulders made me feel gloomy too. Apparently, this was far from the first time something like this had happened.
During the 3 years I'd been absent, there had been discord among my companions that I knew nothing about. I didn't need to ask to picture the hapless Lee Hyunsung caught between them.
I gave Lee Hyunsung a light pat on the shoulder.
I didn't know what had happened, but what I needed to do to understand the situation seemed clear.
“Hyunsung-ssi, where is Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
“······This way.”

It lasted only an instant, but I did not miss the way Lee Hyunsung's expression darkened. After following his broad back for a while, we reached a small door finished with a plain coat of white paint. Unexpectedly, Jung Heewon and Han Sooyoung, whom we'd just parted from, were standing in front of it too.
······What was with these people?
Bewildered, I was about to speak to them when I noticed something odd about their expressions. Jung Heewon was one thing, but I'd never seen Han Sooyoung look like that before.
「Kim Dokja thought. ‘Not a single thing is ea sy.’」
Shut up, you.

With a small sigh, I placed my hand on the doorknob. It seemed that meeting Yoo Sangah first would resolve everything. After a brief knock, just as I tried to open the door, Yoo Sangah's voice came from inside.
―Who is it?
“It's Kim Dokja.”
The reply was unexpected.
―Please leave.
It had been a while since I'd been turned away at the door like that.
I tightened and loosened my grip on the doorknob several times, then glanced behind me.
Jung Heewon's gaze said she was waiting to see what I would do, while Han Sooyoung's was strangely wary. And Lee Hyunsung looked as though he might melt from worry at any moment.
I carefully sat down with my back against the door.
“I won't come in. But could we talk here for a little while?”
This was Yoo Sangah, of all people. If she refused to see me, she must have a good reason. Her answer came only after a long while.
―······All right.
For some reason, her voice sounded weak.
In a silence so deep I could hear everyone breathing, I thought about Yoo Sangah. The Yoo Sangah from when we still worked at Mino Soft.
If someone asked whether I'd been close to Yoo Sangah, I couldn't confidently answer yes.
But if they asked what kind of person Yoo Sangah was······ I might have a little to say about that.
“I'm very late, aren't I?”
I began cautiously.
“I'm sorry. I'm a bit like that. I was late on my first day at work too, and you helped me, Yoo Sangah-ssi······ Do you remember?”
After a moment of silence, Yoo Sangah answered.
―······We were both late that time.
Yoo Sangah might have looked perfect from the outside, but that perfection wasn't something she had been born with. She was more diligent and hardworking than anyone else I knew.
“Do you remember us looking for the interview room together?”
―I remember.

‘Mino Soft’ was fairly well known in the industry for its entry-level job interviews. Each year, the interviews featured a different kind of ‘quest.’ The most common were ‘Raise the Interviewer's Affection’ and ‘Find the Hidden Interview Hints.’
For the record, the quest the year Yoo Sangah and I interviewed was ‘Find the Interview Room.’
―······I think you helped me more than I helped you, Dokja-ssi.
“All I did was find the quest items. You were the one who used them to work out the route, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
Back then, I had teamed up with Yoo Sangah to find the interview room.
―You pointed out how inefficient the quest route was, Dokja-ssi.
“And you pointed out that the quest progression system lacked clear cause and effect, Sangah-ssi.”
Simply clearing the ‘quest’ wasn't the point. Identifying its problems and weaknesses, and assessing its efficiency. That was the core of Mino Soft's entry-level job interviews.
And Yoo Sangah and I had both passed the interview with the highest score.
“It was a shame we ended up in different departments after joining. ······Well, it was only natural.”
Me in QA. And Yoo Sangah in HR.
After we joined the company, we barely managed to exchange greetings in passing.
“I'm happy to be on the same team as you again, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
Very faintly, I heard someone draw in a breath.
“Just like back then, I need you, Yoo Sangah-ssi. I need someone to help me find the way.”
Lee Hyunsung was looking at me with tears welling in his eyes. Jung Heewon let out a small sigh, and Han Sooyoung clicked her tongue and turned her head.
Then I heard Yoo Sangah's voice.
―Dokja-ssi.
“Yes.”
―I'm not that good a person.
For a moment, I didn't know how to answer. I could say with certainty that if Yoo Sangah wasn't a good person, there were no good people in the world.
―Do you remember the break room incident?
Caught off guard, I answered.
“······I remember.”
The incident when someone had sprinkled a whole lot of pepper into the coffee bean container in the company break room.
It had caused an uproar at the company for a while. The bosses had flown into a rage after drinking pepper-flavored coffee, and the innocent new hires had borne the full brunt of their scolding.
―I was the one who did it.
“······Were you?”
―······You don't sound very surprised.
“Thanks to you, the new hires got out of fetching coffee for a while, didn't they?”
The truth was, I'd known Yoo Sangah was the culprit.

The QA employees had been forced to take night shifts to catch the break room culprit. As the team's youngest member, I'd handled most of that duty. I'd been hiding in the break room's cleaning supply cupboard, reading ‘Ways of Survival’ on my smartphone, when I saw Yoo Sangah come in alone in the middle of the night.
―That wasn't the only thing.
Yoo Sangah kept talking.

Most were trivial incidents, yet even those trivial things had brought about small changes. Incidents in which someone had suffered a loss, someone had reclaimed rights they'd lost, and someone else had felt a rush of satisfaction.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
She was not a ‘character.’
But in truth, before ‘Ways of Survival’ arrived, she had seemed more like a ‘character’ to me than anyone else.
Because I'd thought there was no way someone like her could exist in reality.
「“At this rate, she'll die.”」
Yoo Sangah had been like that from the moment the first scenario began.
The only person who had tried to uphold a code of ‘ethics’ that did not exist in ‘Ways of Survival.’
「“I'll do it, Gilyoung. ······Even so, I'll do it.”」
Without Yoo Sangah there, our group would surely have fallen apart.
「“You really say such wonderful things, Dokja-ssi.”」
Without Yoo Sangah, who had met whatever nonsense I said with a smile.
「“Then I have Sangah's life to live.”」
Without her, who had never let go of what needed protecting, no matter what story I created······.
「“I’ve never hated you as much as I do today, Dokja-ssi. Come back. You have to.”」
I would never have been able to make the ‘Otherworld Pledge’ with peace of mind.
―I really couldn't bear it······.
Yoo Sangah's disjointed words continued.
I slowly stood up.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
Yoo Sangah kept talking, as though she couldn't hear my voice.
I listened quietly, then took hold of the doorknob again.
Insisting on helping someone who doesn't want help can be a nuisance.
But some people, even when they clearly need help, cannot bring themselves to ask anyone for it, right to the very end.
Because they have never, not once, asked for anything like that.
······Just like on the day I first went for an interview.
“Wait, Dokja-ssi―!”
I ignored Jung Heewon and forced the locked doorknob to turn. The door creaked as though it would break, and the room beyond came into view. Three people with grim expressions were there.
My eyes met theirs. Lee Seolhwa, Aileen, and······ my mother. My mother's eyes were saying:
You're here.
The three of them stood near the bed. On it lay Yoo Sangah, who had been talking to me all this time. Her face was deathly pale. Her bloodless lips were firmly closed.
Others were doing the talking in her place.
From within Yoo Sangah, broken Stories were flowing out without end.
A little later, I sat down with my companions in Yoo Sangah's sickroom.
“How long has she been like this?”
“······Not long.”
Jung Heewon answered. It was Lee Seolhwa who explained further.
“······She's suffering severe side effects from excessive stigma use.”
I looked down at Yoo Sangah's face, drained of color. If she had had an ordinary constellation sponsor, this would never have happened to her.

Right now, the entire <Olympus> nebula itself was her sponsor. And an irregular <Sponsorship Contract> shortened an incarnation's lifespan. Here, ‘lifespan’ did not simply mean the lifespan of the physical body.
It was the ‘lifespan of a story.’
“Her soul has fallen into a deep sleep beneath her consciousness. All that's left is a 「stream of consciousness」.”

As she repeatedly used stigmas she could not handle, contradictions had accumulated little by little in Yoo Sangah's soul. Probability had created cracks in her body and mind, and eventually, Stories had begun to leak through those cracks.
Aileen added,
“······We've been giving her regular transfusions from Story packs, and we've even gathered the broken fragments and administered them again. But she still isn't improving.”
Watching Yoo Sangah's words drift through the air, I could find nothing to say.
It was all because of me.
Because I had taken too long······.
“······I told you not to go in because I was afraid you'd make that damn face.”
Han Sooyoung said in a grumbling tone.
I bit my lip and looked at Lee Seolhwa.
“How much time does she have?”
“About 3 months······.”
“Isn't there anything we can do?”
“As things stand······ there's nothing we can do here.”
“Then you're saying it might be possible somewhere else.”
[The constellation ‘Guam Divine Doctor’ nods.]
It was Lee Seolhwa's sponsor who responded in her place.
[The constellation ‘Guam Divine Doctor’ says that the illness of incarnation ‘Yoo Sangah’ is not a ‘human illness.’]
Human illnesses could be cured by human power.
······But what if it were an illness of the gods (神)?
[The demon king ‘Demon King of Salvation’ looks up at the night sky.]
Then small stars twinkled here and there in the dark <Star Stream>.
[The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ looks at you.]
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ looks at you.]
They were all stars of <Olympus> connected to Yoo Sangah.
Anger suddenly surged through me.
True, Yoo Sangah herself may have been the one who used the power.
But it was <Olympus> that had induced her to enter such an absurd contract in the first place.
[Olympus, shoulder your own probability.]
I sent my quiet True Voice out into the night sky.
At my words, several stars twinkled again.
[The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’······.]
Tzzzzzzzt!
The next moment, the indirect message cut off in midair amid inexplicable sparks. The shining stars were no longer visible. Someone had interfered with their indirect messages.
I spoke through gritted teeth.
“Those bastards might know a way.”
There was no one here who didn't know who ‘those bastards’ were.
Jung Heewon's expression darkened.
“But there's no way to ask them for help. We've tried something similar so many times, but······.”
Constellations were willful and did only what they wanted.
They watched only the stories they wanted to watch, and listened only to the stories they wanted to hear.
The fact that Yoo Sangah was still in this condition probably meant that the high-ranking constellations did not want a miracle for her.
Han Sooyoung asked,
“What about going to the Underworld like last time? You're close to the Queen of the Underworld.”
“······The circumstances were exceptional that time. And Yoo Sangah-ssi isn't even dead yet. Besides, there's no guarantee it'll turn out like it did with Biyoo.”
In fact, I had been trying to contact Persephone for a while, but there had been no reply.

Even if I reached her, it would still be difficult. When ‘Disaster Shin Yoosung’ reincarnated as Biyoo, we had simply been lucky. In this world, most deaths were literally death. Reincarnation and regression were simply miraculous stories of the <Star Stream>.
“You said Jang Hayoung went off to do another scenario, right?”
“······As far as I know, Hayoung went pretty far away.”
If only Jang Hayoung were here, we could send messages directly to the constellations······.
Looking at Yoo Sangah's sleeping face, I thought and thought.
「A way to save Yoo Sangah.」
In the end, there was only one way.
I drew a slow breath and spoke.
“There is still a way. It's a little earlier than I expected, but······.”
“We must clear scenario 46.”
A man's low, cool voice cut me off.
I frowned and turned toward it.
······Showing up as though you'd been waiting for your cue.
The companions who had been sent out to deal with the Gyeonggi Alliance stood at the door. Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung, Lee Jihye. And······ Yoo Joonghyuk.

The children scurried over and threw themselves into my arms. After stroking Shin Yoosung's head, I glanced at Yoo Joonghyuk, who was glaring at me with a menacing look, then turned back to the others.
“I think it's time we met the constellations.”
“······The constellations?”
A breeze blew through the slightly open window. Dokkaebis were appearing one by one in the distant sky. They had probably come to prepare the next scenario.
Beyond them, the shadows of countless stars flickered as they watched the scenario once more. I pointed to those stars and said,
“Those ‘constellations’ are in the scenario 47 region.”
The scenario 47 region.
There stood the constellations' interstellar city (星間都市), ‘Context of the Constellations.’
“Let's go destroy Olympus.”
A little later, the companions were tending to their equipment as they waited for Kim Dokja. While sharpening her blade, Lee Jihye asked Jung Heewon,
“Do you think Dokja-ajusshi meant it? That he's really going to destroy Olympus······.”
“He must be joking. Dokja-ssi isn't that stupid.”
“But we don't even know where he's been for 3 years. Does he know 3 whole years have passed here?”
“······I'm sure he does. I told you, he's not stupid.”
“But he might have gone crazy during those 3 years we know nothing about. Just look at my master······.”
Lee Jihye abruptly shut her mouth when she felt Yoo Joonghyuk's gaze from afar. Watching her, Jung Heewon heaved a series of sighs and glanced toward the reception room Kim Dokja had entered.
Two people sat in a separate, stark-white room reminiscent of a detention center's visiting room.
“It's been 3 years.”
“······It took longer than I expected.”

Looking at Lee Sookyung, Kim Dokja parted his lips several times. There was much he needed to say, but some words had been buried beneath the accumulated strata of scenarios, while others had missed their moment.
“Um.”
And so, a few words were barely unearthed from the grave of stories past.
“I'm sorry.”
Lee Sookyung smiled faintly.
“You're planning to leave for the next scenario, aren't you?”
“Yes.”
“When?”
“This evening.”
Kim Dokja fell silent for a moment, then asked,
“Will you come with us?”
“There's still a lot I need to do here.”
Lee Sookyung was looking out at the [Industrial Complex] through the reception room window. Kim Dokja followed her gaze outside. There were women there who had once been prisoners of this society.
Cho Gyeongran, whose sponsor was Jeon Woochi. Lee Boksoon, who had fought alongside them in [Peace Land].
“More people than you might think make the wrong choices, pulled along by forces stronger than their own will.”
Those who had once broken the law were now out of prison, fighting for others.
“What matters is that people can change. And perhaps they've finally been given a chance.”
Lee Sookyung's tone was half self-mocking. She turned to look her son in the eyes.
“······You know, don't you? ‘Big stories’ erase individuals.”
“I know.”

Kim Dokja's gaze wavered slightly. Something like tiny sparks flickered in his eyes. Perhaps she shouldn't have brought it up. A person erased by a ‘big story.’ Her son probably knew more about such a person than anyone else in the world. After hesitating for a long time, Lee Sookyung spoke.
“······There was something I wanted to say back then.”
“I know. I read it too.”
The book Lee Sookyung had written, 『Memoir of the Basement Killer』.

As Lee Sookyung's book became a bestseller, society began to discuss domestic violence in earnest, and bills were introduced to strengthen the laws punishing it. So, in the end, viewed on a larger scale, it might have been the right thing to do.
But within that story.
The human beings ‘Lee Sookyung’ and ‘Kim Dokja’ had been completely dissected.

Kim Dokja was cast as the son of a tragedy born of domestic violence in this society, and Lee Sookyung as a criminal who had killed her husband and turned it into a story to tell. People called the two of them by different names. A murderer's son, or a cruel mother······. It was the price of changing the world just a little.
“We were being erased all along, even before that book came out. And maybe we will be from now on, too······.”
Kim Dokja's words broke off before he could finish.
Instead of looking at each other, the two of them were looking out the window.
The world was there.
There was no one who had not been hurt.
Above the heads of incarnations exhausted by the scenarios, constellations shone, wanting stories more terrible still.
Kim Dokja spoke.
“Big stories erase individuals. I'm going to change that.”
“I'm here to change that too.”
“Then······ I suppose we'll part ways here again.”
Kim Dokja rose from his seat and said,
“Stay well.”
Kim Dokja disappeared with the sound of the door closing. Lee Sookyung silently watched the door through which he had gone.
A little later, a shadow stirred behind the reception room curtains, and Han Sooyoung emerged. Looking at the door Kim Dokja had left through, she said,
“······What a cold bastard. Seriously.”
“I raised him that way.”
Han Sooyoung narrowed her eyes at Lee Sookyung's words.
“Ajumma. Why didn't you tell him?”
“Tell him what?”
“About the book.”
Lee Sookyung had a brazen look in her eyes, as though she had no idea what Han Sooyoung meant. Looking at her, Han Sooyoung spoke in a strangely agitated tone.
“I heard everything from your fellow inmates. You sent the royalties from that book to your relatives, didn't you? To help cover his living expenses.”
“None of it actually reached him, so I might as well not have sent it.”
“······Where are those bastard relatives now?”
“They're probably all dead by now.”

Han Sooyoung's half-open mouth closed. Most grudges from before the apocalypse had now become meaningless. Those who should have paid for their sins had all died, free of any worries, while those who remained had to cling to life only to face an even more terrible world.
Han Sooyoung sighed and asked,
“But are you really not coming with us?”
“I feel like I've spent too long raising my child. It's time to leave it at that and live my own life.”
There were more wrinkles on Lee Sookyung's faintly smiling face.

Lee Sookyung was one of the reasons this [Industrial Complex] had been able to function safely. The Demon Realm and Earth. The two different ways of life had been able to coexist peacefully thanks to Lee Sookyung and Yoo Sangah's rule, which made no distinction between them.
Lee Sookyung was indispensable to this [Industrial Complex].
Knowing that well, Han Sooyoung turned away without a word.
Then she strode over and opened the door Kim Dokja had left through.
Lee Sookyung spoke.
“Sooyoung.”
Han Sooyoung raised a hand without looking back.
“Don't worry. Leave your son to me, and you just―”
“Take care of yourself.”

At those words, Han Sooyoung turned back with a blank expression. Lee Sookyung was smiling. Eyes exactly the same color as Kim Dokja's. Han Sooyoung's lips parted, and she spoke in something like a sigh.
“Honestly······ insufferable to the very end.”
A young girl sucking on a piece of candy suddenly pointed at me and declared,
“Squid.”
The sudden mental attack left me dazed for a moment.
[Some constellations are curious about the girl's identity.]
As for who this girl was······ well······ I sighed and said her name.
“Mia, have you been well?”
“Who are you, ajusshi?”
It seemed she had forgotten me again because we hadn't seen each other in so long.
I was about to explain when Yoo Mia clapped her hands and said,
“Ah, my elder brother's friend.”
“We're not friends······ You've changed the way you talk since I last saw you.”
“You've gotten even uglier since I last saw you, ajusshi.”
“Hey, Yoo Joonghyuk. You're not planning to bring your sister too, are you?”
At my words, Yoo Joonghyuk, who had a hand planted on Yoo Mia's head, glared at me.
I looked at him for a moment, then asked awkwardly,
“······Have you been well? Things were so hectic I forgot to ask.”
“There is no time for idle questions like that.”
Strangely, hearing that stiff voice felt familiar rather than unpleasant. Yes, this was the Yoo Joonghyuk I knew.
The Yoo Joonghyuk I knew continued,
“Scenario 46 is dangerous. Of course I'm leaving my sister behind.”
“Who else are you leaving here? Yoo Sangah-ssi obviously has no choice but to stay, and then there's my mother and the ‘wanderers’······.”
“I'm leaving the Flying Fox here.”
“You've already talked to the Flying Fox?”
“I made a contract with the returnee group.”

The returnees, now freed from being disasters, would need some time to adjust to their home world. Yoo Joonghyuk had already contacted them, made a contract concerning the protection of the [Industrial Complex], and returned. As expected of the protagonist, his ability to get things done was incredible.
But I shook my head.
“They can't protect this place on their own.”
“My master will return here soon as well.”
“That's not the problem. Besides, it's even more dangerous if transcendents are here. You know that, right?”
Yoo Joonghyuk would know exactly what I meant.
After all, he had already lost the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint in a previous round.
Yoo Joonghyuk nodded.
“I know. We just need to return before ‘that’ happens. You should focus on scenario 46.”
“I am.”
“It won't be easy. We may fail.”
It wasn't strange for him to say that.
―You can't clear scenario 46 alone. You know that, don't you?
On the day I first met Yoo Joonghyuk, I had said those words to persuade him.
And at last, the day had come to make those words a reality.
Yoo Joonghyuk said,
“There are several ways to clear scenario 46.”
“No, there's only one.”
“It won't go the way you think.”
“Did you even talk much with the others while I was gone?”
“I don't trust people.”
As Yoo Joonghyuk answered coldly, Yoo Mia nodded along beside him, listening.
“You know what comes after 46, don't you? From now on, unless you cooperate with other people―”
“True disasters don't show on the surface.”
I fell silent at Yoo Joonghyuk's words.
Scenario 45, ‘Glorious Return,’ had been a scenario about fighting ‘disasters.’
A battle against beings who looked like monsters on the outside but were human on the inside.
I read the messages saved in the system log.
[You have cleared scenario 45.]
[None of your group members died throughout the scenario.]
[Your group members did not kill any incarnations throughout the scenario.]
[Your group has demonstrated a new possibility between incarnations and returnees!]
[You and your group members are released from ‘Disaster’ status.]
A new possibility. It was proof that trust and faith were possible even between species with different appearances. As though he had read my thoughts, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“Since the scenarios began, many people have fallen victim to them. But even more people have died at the hands of their fellow humans.”
Yoo Joonghyuk, his cold eyes gleaming, suddenly seemed far away.
“You will lose your companions in this scenario.”
“Why are you talking as if this has nothing to do with you······.”
“I've already lost many people. But I suppose it's different for you.”
“You would do well to prepare yourself.”

I frowned. I knew what scenario 46 was too. That was why I couldn't readily accept what Yoo Joonghyuk was saying. The companions I knew would never do such a thing. Sure, they were the sort of people who would lock me up and feed me sleeping pills after seeing me for the first time in 3 years, but they would never fight or quarrel with each other······.
“By the way, are you coming too?”
“Yeah. Why?”
“······Oh, I was just asking.”
······I could see fierce sparks flying in the air.

In the distance, I saw the others approaching. Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung were at the front, with Lee Jihye, Lee Hyunsung, and Lee Seolhwa walking behind them in that order. The problem was Jung Heewon and Han Sooyoung, who were in their midst.
······Come to think of it, those two did have a problem. Damn it.
[Main Scenario #46 ― ‘Proof of the Stars’ has arrived!]
Main scenario 46, Proof of the Stars.
To meet <Olympus> and the other constellation bastards, we had to clear this scenario.
Tzzzzzt······!
Before long, the dokkaebis who would run the scenario appeared in midair.
[We will now begin the main scenario.]
The dokkaebi who appeared for the scenario wasn't Bihyung. But it was a very familiar dokkaebi. One who had once been a low-grade dokkaebi, and had even learned how to use the Dokkaebi Bag from me.
―······Kim Dokja-nim?
The dokkaebi, eyes as wide as oil lamps, contacted me through Dokkaebi Communication.
―It's me! Youngki, the dokkaebi!
Youngki, dressed in a suit, was looking at me. Perhaps because he was running the main scenario, he seemed reluctant to let the other participants notice.
―It's been a while.
―I heard rumors that you'd returned······.
―······Word has already spread?
―Oh, how could I not know? Bihyung-nim is running all over the place right now, trying to sort out the probability you threw into chaos, Kim Dokja-nim······.
Youngki grinned and continued.
―Anyway, it's good to see you again. The other constellations have been asking about you a lot too, Dokja-nim. Once this scenario is over, you'll finally be going to meet your supporters.
―If things go well.
―Hehe, of course they will. But there'll be no special treatment, even for you, Kim Dokja-nim. You understand, don't you?
―I know.
I heard murmuring in the distance. Before I knew it, quite a few incarnations had gathered nearby to participate in scenario 46.
[Hmm······ 48 in total. The Seoul region has relatively few participants.]
Youngki's tone had changed, and he calmly surveyed the applicants.
The applicants were all different in appearance.

Some were people who had been residents of the [Industrial Complex] from the start, while others were incarnations who had desperately fought their way through the scenarios to reach this point. I also saw a few returnees who, though freed from being disasters, had rejected Yoo Joonghyuk's contract.
Faces twisted with deep sorrow and rage.
They were probably people who had failed to find their families back home.
[This scenario is very different from the scenarios so far. First, this is a ‘choice-based scenario.’]
A returnee from Murim raised a question.
“A choice-based scenario? What's that?”
[It means you can choose whether to participate as an ‘individual’ or as a ‘nebula.’ Well, whichever you choose, you will need at least one companion to participate with you.]
As I listened to Youngki's voice, I quietly clenched and unclenched my fist.
Scenario 46, ‘Proof of the Stars.’
I felt that what was bound to come had finally come.
I could hear the incarnations whispering.
“What? What's the difference between participating as an individual and participating as a nebula?”
“Idiot. Participating as an individual literally means going alone, and participating as a nebula must mean going as a group. Well, assuming you have a nebula.”
“What happens to people who've already joined a nebula? Are they forced to participate ‘as a nebula’?”
[Oh, you've asked a very important question. As it happens, on that subject······.]
Just as Youngki was about to continue, shafts of light flashed across the night sky.
[Oh dear, you're here already. How impatient you all are.]
At those words, messages poured from the air.
The messages descended toward their destinations like shooting stars, circling above the incarnations' heads and radiating brilliant light.
[The nebula <Asgard> invites you.]
[The nebula <Guardian Tree> invites you.]
[The nebula <Tamna> invites you.]
[The nebula <Emperor> invites you.]
Scenario 46 began with a recruitment contest among the nebulas.
“Wh-what is this?!”

The startled incarnations cried out. I also saw some studying their lists of nebulas with thoughtful expressions. They were the few returnees who already knew about the scenario. Some incarnations even counted the stars circling above other people's heads. Most had one or two, while some had more than five.
“······Holy shit, what's going on over there?”

Of course, our group had received the most messages. In particular, the radiance around several of my companions, including Yoo Joonghyuk, was so intense that their faces were practically impossible to see.
I looked up above my head.
[You have received a total of 137 nebula invitations.]
[However, accepting one of these invitations will automatically dissolve the nebula <Kim Dokja’s Company>.]
Were they sending these messages just to poke holes in a persimmon they couldn't eat?
Did they really think I would dissolve my own nebula and join theirs?
Once the incarnations seemed to have calmed down a little, Youngki continued.
[This is the first scenario in which you will be chosen by a <nebula>. You may join one of the <nebulas> that invited you and participate in the scenario.]
“Do we have to join? What's so good about joining?”
[You are free not to join. However, if the <nebula> you join has already completed scenario 46, ‘Proof of the Stars’······.]
Youngki smiled slyly.
[You will be exempted from this scenario and may proceed directly to scenario 47.]
Amid the commotion of the incarnations, my companions gathered around me one by one.
“I'll choose <Emperor>!”
“I'll take <Flag of Glory>.”
Even then, incarnations who had made their choices were shouting here and there.
[Please be aware before making your choice that anyone who selects a nebula that qualifies for the exemption will automatically be transported to region 47.]

Most incarnations chose to be carried through by a nebula rather than attempt scenario 46. It was a reasonable decision, to a degree. The Korean Peninsula had been progressing through the scenarios relatively slowly, so scenario 46 had already become quite notorious through other countries where it had taken place earlier.
―When two people attempt scenario 46, one dies.
None of them wanted to be the one who died.
Some incarnations postponed their participation, while others accepted the nebulas' invitations and moved on to the next scenario.
The number of incarnations dwindled, and at last, Youngki looked at us.
[Now you're the only ones left. What will you do?]
The companions gathered around me were waiting for my choice.
Youngki asked again.
[Will you apply as a nebula or as individuals? Well, whichever you choose, you cannot apply alone.]
“If we pass this scenario as a nebula, anyone who belongs to the same nebula afterward will automatically be advanced to the next scenario, right?”
[Oh, that's correct, ‘Demon King of Salvation’-nim. Are you planning to attempt it as a nebula?]
“Yes.”

Scenario 46, ‘Proof of the Stars,’ was essentially a debut stage for a newly formed nebula like ours. The Story recorded in ‘Context of the Constellations’ would differ according to how many casualties we suffered and what results we achieved in this scenario.
I turned to my companions.
None of my companions apart from Yoo Joonghyuk and me had joined a nebula yet.
After meeting each companion's gaze, I took a slow breath and spoke.
“I won't dictate your choice. But bear this in mind. If you choose another nebula here and proceed with the scenarios, you will certainly face unfair restrictions―”
“You really can't be honest, Dokja-ajusshi. Why don't you just ask us to join?”
Lee Jihye cut me off, jutting out her lips. As the others clicked their tongues at me, Jung Heewon was the first to speak.
“Hmm, what should I do?”
An overwhelming number of ‘nebula invitations’ glittered above Jung Heewon's head as she smiled playfully.
“Considering Uriel, I really ought to go to <Eden>······.”

In fact, incarnations usually joined the nebula their sponsor belonged to. But there were certainly sponsors who were very open-minded or respected their incarnation's individual choices. <Eden> in particular tended to respect incarnations' free will in that regard.
Jung Heewon asked,
“Does <Kim Dokja’s Company> enroll us in all 4 major social insurance programs?”
“Uh, well. This is my first time running something like this······.”
“What about lunch breaks and nap time?”
“How much time do we get for personal upkeep?”
“What about supplies of medicinal ingredients and materials?”
Lee Jihye, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Seolhwa. Each asked the questions they wanted to ask.
“Well, you see······ as you know, <Kim Dokja’s Company> is a newly formed nebula that's only just been established.”
After stumbling over my words amid the barrage of questions, I sighed and continued.

“You'll all have to decide your own breaks and time for personal upkeep. I'll do my best to supply consumable materials, but there may not be enough. You may have to work late often, and I may not be able to pay you enough for it.”
Even as I said it, I thought I was being shameless.

Even so, Lee Hyunsung was listening attentively, while Lee Jihye was yawning.
“And that's not all······.”
“Dokja-ssi.”
“Yes?”

“Honestly, there's a mountain of things I want to ask you. Where you've been all this time, what you were doing that made you take so long to come back.”

Perhaps it wasn't only Jung Heewon.

That stalwart swordswoman was looking at me with faintly reddened eyes.

“Thank you, Heewon-ssi.”

“There is a great deal I want to say too······ but Heewon-ssi has said it all.”

Splitting up the group because there were too many of us?
There hadn't been anything like that in scenario 46 in the original novel?

―I'm sorry, Kim Dokja-nim.

······These fucking bastards. So you're going to get in our way to the very end?
